name: Saptam Patel
bio: Saptam Patel is an Associate Professor in the area of Communication at Ahmedabad University, with specialisation in Gender Studies and interdisciplinary learning. With over two decades of academic experience, her work reflects a sustained commitment to integrating humanities, social sciences, and experiential learning into contemporary higher education. Her contributions extend beyond teaching into institutional leadership, curriculum design, and the development of innovative pedagogical frameworks aligned with the University’s mission. Her research area is multidisciplinary as she has been working on literature in English, gender, fine arts and women's writing, and she has published/presented and participated in various international and national conferences and seminars.

She did her Fine Arts study at Sheth C N College of Fine Arts, Ahmedabad. She has been a member of a group of women artists called 'Expressive Eight' and exhibited at Jehangir Art Gallery, Rabindra Bhavan, Ravishankar Raval Kala Bhavan, Marvel Art Gallery, Hutheesingh Visual Art Gallery, Contemporary Art Gallery – Ahmedabad, Chandigarh at international galleries. She has participated in almost twenty national and international shows of paintings, prints, and photographs.
Over 25 years of experience in teaching, academic administration, and institution building
Expertise in Gender Studies, Communication, and interdisciplinary pedagogy
Key contributor to the design and execution of the Foundation Programme
Strong engagement with curriculum development and policy formulation
Active involvement in student-centric initiatives and academic leadership roles

teaching: Saptam Patel’s teaching philosophy emphasizes critical inquiry, interdisciplinary thinking, and real-world engagement. His courses are designed to move beyond disciplinary silos, encouraging students to connect theory with lived experience.
An interdisciplinary foundation course that investigates water as a complex global issue through integrated perspectives of society, environment, and policy
Feminism is for Everybody - First Year Interdisciplinary Seminar Course on Critical Thinking and Writing
Introduces foundational feminist ideas and practices, fostering critical engagement with questions of equality, power, and lived experience across diverse contexts
Beyond Pink and Blue: Redefining Masculinity and Femininity - Independent Study Period Course
Challenges conventional gender binaries by critically examining constructs of masculinity and femininity through theory and lived experience
WWW: Window to the World of Water - Independent Study Period Course
Introduces an interdisciplinary understanding of water by connecting environmental, social, and cultural perspectives through exploratory learning
Quotidian Story of Gender - Engagement and Application based Learning and Education - ENABLE Course
Engages with everyday experiences to unpack how gender operates across social, cultural, and personal dimensions in contemporary life

paragraphs: Foundation Programme | Professor Saptam Patel, shares her impressions of the Foundation Programme, which is driven by project-based learning. The Programme integrates disciplines to enrich learning and shape students into independent thinkers.
In Conversation with Saptam Patel, Ahmedabad University

The Story Of Water: How This Shapeless Substance Has Shaped Society - In this session of Ahmedabad University’s Conversation Series, Dr Giulio Boccaletti is Honorary Research Associate, Smith School of Enterprise and the Environment, Oxford University, Senior Fellow, Euro-Mediterranean Center for Climate Change, Italy, and Former Chief Strategy Officer and Global Ambassador for Water, Nature Conservancy speaks on ‘The Story Of Water: How This Shapeless Substance Has Shaped Society’ He takes us through how humanity's relationship to moving water has shaped civilisation, transformed political institutions, and defined people's lives. He will provide an interdisciplinary perspective by bringing cosmology, mythology, archaeology, and history to illustrate how human civilisation is shaped by water.
